# Charter

This repository is governed by a charter — the standards it authored under `.cw/charter/`, which constrain whatever coding agent runs here. Every surface an agent reads, this file included, is generated from that charter: do not edit them, edit the primitive behind them.

## Read first

Read [catalogue.json](./catalogue.json) for shared primitives and `catalogue.<provider>.json` linked from your agent's entry file for primitives restricted to your provider. Entries are not repeated between these files. Each entry lists kind, id, description, file and globs. Use these two catalogues and open a file when its activation condition below is met.

## When each kind applies

- **guide** — a touched file matches one of its `globs`, or every turn where globs are not specified.
- **sensor** — the `signal` it names is raised, and the harness runs what it says to `run`.
- **skill** — one of its `triggers` matches what is being asked.
- **playbook** — one of its `triggers` matches; the body is a sequence of skills.
- **agent** — it is spawned by id, holding the `tools` it lists and nothing else — an mcp origin as `[[<id>]]`, or one of its tools as `[[<id>]]:<tool>`.
- **posture** — always, wherever the agent can be told what to `allow` and what to `deny`.
- **corpus** — a primitive's `rationale` cites it — the reasoning, read when someone asks why.
- **mixin** — never on its own: its body is lent to the primitives that pull it in.
- **mcp** — a primitive's body names it as `[[<id>]]` — an mcp origin outside the repository, reached through `cw run mcp`.
- **script** — a primitive names it as `[[<id>]]`, or a sensor runs it — its assets, copied to `./script/<id>/`, of which its `executionPath` names the one to run.
- **template** — a primitive names it as `[[<id>]]` — a file the agent fills or copies, written as its body.

## One id, one primitive

An id names one primitive in the whole charter, whatever its kind: it is all a primitive is named by — bare in a header, a test or a command, and as `[[<id>]]` in a body, a sensor's `run` or an agent's `tools` — whether this repository authored it, installed it from a charter source, or the engine brought it. Nothing overrides anything — two files claiming one id is an error the charter refuses to build with.

files..cw/out/skill/charter-release/index.md:
---
kind: skill
id: charter-release
description: For publishing a new version of the charters this repository authored, so other repositories can install or update them, with nothing pushed before you confirm.
triggers: ["release", "release a version", "cut a release"]
disable-model-invocation: true
---

This skill is cw's own. It comes with the engine to every repository, is
not authored in this repository, and cannot be changed here.

Release the charters this repository authored the way [charter-release-action](../../script/charter-release-action/index.md)
says. Each step below runs its `charter-release-action.mjs`, the file laid
beside it, with `node` by that file's path. Nothing is committed, pushed or
tagged before the user confirms at the gate.

1. **Check** — run `charter-release-action.mjs check`. Where it stops, quote what it
   says and stop: a branch other than `origin`'s default branch, a working
   tree that is not clean, no `origin`, the branch behind or diverged from
   `origin`, or a charter that does not build with the charters it includes
   alone, named with why. Where it says it is unsure which branch to release
   from, ask the user which branch releases are made from, proposing the branch
   it names, the one stood on, and run
   `charter-release-action.mjs check --branch <name>` with their answer; pass
   that same `--branch` to publish.
2. **Draft** — run `charter-release-action.mjs draft`, which writes nothing. Where it
   says there is nothing to release, say so and stop; where the last tag and
   the top heading of the changelog, `.cw/CHANGELOG.md`, differ, quote both
   and stop.
   - **Version**: `0.1.0` where there is no tag. Otherwise the patch bump,
     or the minor bump where what landed breaks a repository already
     installing a charter of it — a charter or a primitive removed or
     renamed, an id changed, a skill or a command a user types gone — said
     with its reason. Where the user named a version or a date, take it, and
     say so only where it is not what the changes call for; run
     `charter-release-action.mjs draft` again with `--version <version>`, and
     `--date <date>` where they named one, and where it stops, quote what it
     says and ask for another.
   - **Entry**: one bullet per change a user of a charter notices, from the
     commits it lists, in the voice of the changelog's earlier entries: what a
     user can now do, or what changed for them. Leave out what changes only
     this repository's tooling.
3. **Gate** — show the version with its reason, the date, the entry as it
   will read under `## <version> — <date>`, and that the README's install and
   charters section is written from the charters. Ask one question: confirm,
   or correct the version, the date or the entry. On a correction of the
   version or the date, run
   `charter-release-action.mjs draft --version <version> --date <date>`, and
   where it stops, quote what it says and ask again; show the correction and
   ask again, until they confirm.
4. **README** — only once they confirm, run
   `charter-release-action.mjs readme`. Where it stops, quote what it says and
   stop. It rewrites only the install and charters section of `README.md`,
   writing `README.md` holding that section alone where there is no
   `README.md`, and putting the section at its end where the README holds
   none; the rest is the authors' and is never touched.
5. **Release** — then write the entry to a temporary file
   outside the repository, and run
   `charter-release-action.mjs publish <version> <entry-file> --date <date>`,
   with the `--branch` the user confirmed at Check, if any. Where it
   stops, quote its lines as they are — the step that failed, the steps that
   ran, the command that finishes the rest — and do nothing more: never
   force-push, never move or delete a tag.
6. **Report** — the version released, and the tag `v<version>` on `origin`.

files..cw/out/script/charter-release-action/in:
---
kind: script
id: charter-release-action
description: For releasing the charters this repository authored the same way every time — the steps of /charter-release that must not depend on the agent's judgement.
executionPath: ./charter-release-action.mjs
---

This script is cw's own. It comes with the engine to every repository, is
not authored in this repository, and cannot be changed here.

The steps of `/charter-release` that a script takes. It is
`charter-release-action.mjs`, the file laid beside this one: run it with Node 20
or later and nothing else, by that file's path, from anywhere in the
repository, since it runs at the repository's root. Which version, and what
the changelog says, are never its to decide.

```bash
node <the path of charter-release-action.mjs> check [--branch <name>]
node <the path of charter-release-action.mjs> readme
node <the path of charter-release-action.mjs> draft [--version x.y.z] [--date yyyy-mm-dd]
node <the path of charter-release-action.mjs> publish <version> <entry-file> [--date yyyy-mm-dd] [--branch <name>]
```

The release branch is `origin`'s default branch, the one its `HEAD` names,
whatever it is called: `main`, `develop` or another. Where `origin` names
no default branch — it holds no commit yet — it is never guessed: **check** and
**publish** stop, naming the branch stood on, until the branch the user confirms
is passed as `--branch <name>`; an `origin` that cannot be reached stops them,
saying so. A `--branch` other than `origin`'s default branch is
refused.

A charter the repository authored is a folder under `.cw/charter/` that git
holds, holding no `cw-package.json`; one holding it was installed, and is not
released here.

- **check** stops, writing nothing, unless the branch stood on is the release
  branch, the working tree is clean, the branch has an `origin` and is neither
  behind nor diverged from it there, and git ignores no file under
  `.cw/charter/`, which no install would hold; then it runs `cw build` at the root, and
  stops naming each charter that does not build, with what the build said, or
  naming what the build changed of what is committed. No
  primitive may hold or name what cw builds into every repository to release
  charters, so a
  charter building here builds with the charters it includes alone.
- **readme** rewrites the section of `README.md` between
  `<!-- charter-release-action: charters -->` and `<!-- /charter-release-action: charters -->`
  from the charters as built: the `cw charter pull <address>` that
  installs every charter the repository authored, naming each with
  `--charter=<name>` so that none it installed is taken with them but one
  an authored charter includes, the address the one `origin` names, a
  credential an `https://` address carries left out, then for
  each charter the repository authored, the `--charter=<name>` that installs it
  alone and a table of its skills with their descriptions, and last a link to
  `.cw/CHANGELOG.md`, the changelog of these charters. A skill is listed
  when it is kept under the charter's `primitive/skill/`; cw's own skills, such
  as `cw-author`, are left out. The rest of `README.md` is left as it is;
  where there is no `README.md`, it is written holding that section alone,
  and where it holds no section, the section is put at its end; one holding
  one of the two lines alone, or the two out of order, is refused.
  A `README.md` holding the section under the markers an earlier
  `/vendor-release` wrote is refused, naming the markers to rename.
- **draft** reads the last release, the highest `v<version>` tag, and stops
  unless `.cw/CHANGELOG.md`, where it is there, opens with `# Changelog` and
  its top `## ` heading names it. It prints `0.1.0` with no tag, else the patch and the minor bump after
  it, what was removed or renamed under `.cw/charter/`, today's date and every
  commit since; with none, it says there is nothing to release. With
  `--version` or `--date`, it first refuses them as **publish** would: no
  version, a tag already there, a version not after the last release, no date.
- **publish** writes the entry the file holds as `## <version> — <date>`
  under `# Changelog` in `.cw/CHANGELOG.md`, writing it where it is not
  there and never reading a `CHANGELOG.md` at the root, commits
  it with what `readme` changed as `release v<version>`, pushes the release branch, makes the annotated tag `v<version>`
  and pushes it, in that order. It stops, writing nothing, where anything
  but `README.md` and `.cw/CHANGELOG.md` changed since check. It
  stops at the first step that fails, quoting its decisive line, saying which
  steps ran and the command that finishes the rest. It never force-pushes, and
  never moves or deletes a tag.

---
kind: skill
id: cw-author
description: Author a new primitive of this repository's charter, asking cw what its kind requires.
triggers: ["write a rule", "add a standard", "write a skill", "author a primitive of the charter"]
---

# Authoring a primitive of this charter

This skill is cw's own. It comes with the engine, is not authored in this
repository, and cannot be changed here. A repository that wants another way of
authoring writes a primitive of its own, under an id of its own.

It covers writing a new primitive. Changing or removing one that already exists
is not what it covers.

Do not write a primitive from memory, or copy the headers of another one. What a
kind requires is asked of cw, which answers from the same contract a file is
refused against.

1. If the kind is not settled, run `cw kinds`. It names every kind and when a
   primitive of each comes up; take the one whose line matches what is being
   asked for.
2. Run `cw kinds <kind>`. It names every header that kind requires, the shape
   each takes — one line, or a list — the values one drawn from a closed set
   may hold, and a sample written in full.
3. Run `cw add <kind> <id> --charter=<charter> --header <name>=<value>`, one
   `--header` for each header step 2 named, and for any other the sample
   shows this primitive needs. `<charter>` is one the repository authored,
   which `cw add` names when it is refused for want of one, or a new one the
   developer names. A header that takes a list is given once per entry, in order; one that
   takes a line is given once. Everything after the first `=` is the value. If
   cw refuses, it says why and shows the kind's sample: answer again with that
   in hand. Nothing is written until the headers hold.
4. Write the body into the file cw named. The headers decide when the primitive
   comes up; the body is what an agent reads once it has. Name another
   primitive by its id alone: bare in a header, and as `[[<id>]]` in the
   body, which the build turns into a link to it. An id names one primitive
   whatever its kind.
5. Run `cw build`. If it refuses, `cw doctor` names each file with a problem
   and how to fix it.

## Moving a charter laid out the old way

When cw refuses a command because the repository is laid out the old way, ask
the developer which charter the repository's own primitives go in: a name
written as an id is, and never a kind's, `primitive`, `test`, `eval`,
`vendor` or `root`. Then, before anything else, move every
file below, keeping its contents as they are, `<charter>` being the name
answered. First, a `.cw/eval/.worktrees/` an evaluation left is not moved:
delete it, then run `git worktree prune`. Then move:

- `.cw/charter/<kind>/` → `.cw/charter/<charter>/primitive/<kind>/`, for each kind's folder right under `.cw/charter/`
- `.cw/charter/primitive/<kind>/` → `.cw/charter/<charter>/primitive/<kind>/`, for each kind's folder right under `.cw/charter/primitive/`
- `.cw/test/` → `.cw/charter/<charter>/test/`
- `.cw/charter/test/` → `.cw/charter/<charter>/test/`
- `.cw/eval/` → `.cw/charter/<charter>/eval/`
- `.cw/charter/eval/` → `.cw/charter/<charter>/eval/`

An installed charter under `.cw/vendor/` or `.cw/charter/vendor/` is never moved: name
each to the developer, and ask them to delete the folder; never delete it
yourself. Once the repository builds, each
is installed again with a cw of 1.4.0 or later, `cw charter pull <source>`, from a
source laid out as that cw reads one.

A skill `vendor-release` and a script `vendor-release-action` that an
earlier cw wrote are not moved: name them to the developer, and ask them to
delete them, since `/charter-release` comes with cw and replaces them; never
delete them yourself.

`.cw/settings.json` and what a build put out stay where they are. In
`.cw/.gitignore`, the line `eval/.worktrees/`
becomes `log/`. Then run `cw build`: it builds what it built before the
move, but for the installed charters deleted.

This script is cw's own. It comes with the engine, is not authored in this
repository, and cannot be changed here.

Run when the agent stops, with Claude Code's Stop event on its standard input,
it counts the session's tokens so far — input, output, written to and read from
the cache — subagents included, off Claude Code's own transcript of the
session. Each stop is kept as one line of
`<session id>/session-analysis.jsonl`, on this machine: under
`~/.cherry-works/<the repository's path>/`, each character of the path that is
not a letter or a digit written as a dash, or in the `sessionAnalysisFolder`
of `.cw/settings.json`. Nothing is committed or sent
anywhere.

When the session crosses a mark — every 100,000 tokens, or the
`sessionContextMark` of `.cw/settings.json` — the developer is shown one line with
its tokens. The model is sent nothing of it.

A transcript it cannot read is left alone: nothing is shown or kept, and the
agent stops as it would have.
